title: ₹25,000 Monthly Savings: Balancing SIPs, Stocks, and FDs for Growth
description: Effectively investing ₹25,000 monthly requires a balanced approach considering your financial goals and risk tolerance. Systematic Investment Plans (SIPs) in .

faq.q: How much should I allocate to each asset class?
faq.a: There's no fixed rule; it depends entirely on your financial goals, investment horizon, and personal risk tolerance. A common guideline is to allocate a higher percentage to equities for long-term goals and a higher percentage to FDs or debt for short-term goals.

faq.q: Are SIPs better than lump sum investments?
faq.a: SIPs are generally recommended for retail investors as they average out the purchase cost over time (rupee-cost averaging) and promote investment discipline, mitigating the risk of timing the market. Lump sum investments are suitable if you have a large corpus and strong market conviction.

faq.q: What are the tax implications of these investments?
faq.a: Interest from FDs is fully taxable as per your income tax slab. Long-term capital gains from equity mutual funds and stocks (held over 1 year) are taxed at 10% on gains exceeding ₹1 lakh in a financial year. Short-term capital gains (held less than 1 year) are taxed at 15%.

faq.q: How often should I review my portfolio?
faq.a: It's advisable to review your portfolio at least once a year, or whenever there's a significant change in your financial situation (e.g., a new job, marriage, birth of a child) or market conditions. This helps ensure your allocation remains aligned with your goals.

faq.q: Can I invest in direct stocks if I am a beginner?
faq.a: While direct stock investing can offer high returns, it requires significant research and understanding of market dynamics. Beginners might find it safer to start with diversified equity mutual fund SIPs, which are professionally managed, before venturing into direct equities.

faq.q: Should I prioritise building an emergency fund or investing?
faq.a: Always prioritise building an emergency fund first, covering 3-6 months of essential expenses, in easily accessible instruments like FDs or liquid funds. This provides a financial safety net before you commit to long-term investments.
